answers: Why does 'from sklearn.model_selection import *' raise an ImportError?

Constraints: Only apply when downstream routines accept int64 indices (like eigsh); keep accept_large_sparse=False when passing data to Cython/C code requiring 32-bit index buffers.

proposed.title: Avoid division by zero on line search step stagnation in Newton solver
answers: Why does Newton solver raise a divide by zero warning during line search?

Root cause: In sklearn/linear_model/_glm/_newton_solver.py:NewtonSolver, when step size alpha hits min_step_length and stagnates (alpha == alpha_old), subsequent trial step calculations divide by denom = 0.
Fix pattern: Break early when alpha == alpha_old and track convergence with an explicit boolean flag so that non-convergent early termination still triggers the solver's failure warning.
Constraints: Applies to iterative step-size backtracking bounded by a minimum step length; does not apply if step updates cannot stagnate at equal successive values.

proposed.title: Check sorted weights instead of original sample weights during percentile averaging
answers: Why does _weighted_percentile return NaN at percentile rank 100 when average=True?

Root cause: sklearn/utils/stats.py:_weighted_percentile indexed into the original sample_weight instead of sorted_weights when checking if the next rank had zero weight, bypassing zeroed-out NaN weights.
Fix pattern: Check zero-weight adjacent positions against sorted_weights using sorted indices (percentile_plus_one_indices) rather than indexing original sample_weight.
Constraints: Applies when weights are reordered or modified (such as zeroing weights for NaNs) prior to computing CDF lookahead; does not apply when weights remain unsorted or unmodified.

Constraints: Applies when caching signatures or inspect metadata on instance hooks; not applicable when hooks are already standalone functions.

answers: Why do classification metrics fail when given pandas Series and array API predictions?

proposed.title: Mixed device and string label array API handling in LinearDiscriminantAnalysis
answers: How do I support mixed device or namespace array API inputs in scikit-learn estimators?
Why does LinearDiscriminantAnalysis.fit crash when y is on a different device or has string labels?
How does the 'everything follows X' policy handle string labels with array API devices?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Fitting LinearDiscriminantAnalysis with array API inputs raises when y resides on a different device or namespace than X, or when y contains string labels.
Root cause: sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py:LinearDiscriminantAnalysis.fit did not align y to X's device or namespace, and array API standards cannot represent non-numeric string labels.
Fix pattern: Extract self.classes_ using unique_labels(y), encode y into integer codes with _encode, and transfer the codes to X's namespace and device using move_to before passing them to solvers.
Constraints: Applies to array-API-compliant estimators following the 'everything follows X' policy; self.classes_ must remain in y's original device/namespace.
proposed.applies: Array API input validation and device alignment in scikit-learn classification estimators.

proposed.title: Target pre-encoding invariant for LinearDiscriminantAnalysis internal helpers
answers: What input format do _class_means and _class_cov expect for target y in LinearDiscriminantAnalysis?
Why do LinearDiscriminantAnalysis solvers pass y_encoded and n_classes to internal helpers?
How to compute class means and covariances with pre-encoded targets in LinearDiscriminantAnalysis?
proposed.body:
Invariant: Internal class statistic helpers require targets pre-encoded as zero-based integer codes indexing self.classes_, accompanied by an explicit keyword-only n_classes parameter.
Where enforced: Enforced in sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py:_class_means and sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py:_class_cov.
Consequences: Passing raw labels or omitting n_classes breaks group indexing (y_encoded == idx) and bincount operations, causing shape mismatches or silent mean corruption.
